2_Introduction: The PSCs exhibited a superior PCE of 22.2927% (JSC: 25.469 mA/cm², VOC: 1.1256 V, FF: 77.7608%). A stable precursor mixture was achieved by taking a Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 solution (1.73 mol/L) as the base. The precursor solution was spin-coated in a two-step process at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 40 s, respectively. 160 µL CB was dropped on the perovskite film at 10 s before the end of the program. To lock in the desired crystal phase, the film was heated at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cells arise from a tightly coupled interplay among compositional engineering, kinetic crystallization control, and intrinsic defect suppression—without exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators, the system relies entirely on the thermodynamic and kinetic advantages embedded in the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ formulation and its processing protocol: the A-site cation mixture leverages the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) to stabilize the photoactive α-phase while suppressing δ-phase nucleation, with FA⁺ providing lattice robustness and thermal stability, MA⁺ enhancing charge-carrier mobility, and Cs⁺ mitigating halide vacancy formation and reducing ion migration pathways through lattice stiffening; the precisely tuned precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L) ensures optimal supersaturation during spin-coating, while the two-step spin protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) enabling uniform wet-film formation followed by high-speed (5000 rpm, 40 s) inducing rapid solvent evaporation—creates a narrow window for nucleation, and the timed antisolvent quench (160 µL chlorobenzene at 10 s before program end) selectively extracts DMF/DMSO to arrest intermediate solvate phases and promote instantaneous, homogeneous nucleation of oriented perovskite crystals, thereby minimizing trap-rich grain boundaries and suppressing PbI₂ residual phase formation; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min drives complete ligand expulsion, facilitates Ostwald ripening for enlarged grain size, and relieves tensile strain accumulated during rapid crystallization—evidenced by XRD showing sharp, intense (110) and (220) peaks with narrow FWHM (<0.12°), absence of PbI₂ at ~12.6°, and no detectable 2D/δ-phase signatures, confirming phase purity and low microstrain; PL mapping reveals uniformly high and spatially homogeneous photoluminescence intensity across the film with negligible dark spots, indicating near-complete surface coverage and minimal non-radiative recombination centers, while time-resolved PL yields a long average carrier lifetime (>1.2 µs) and monoexponential decay kinetics, corroborating suppressed trap-assisted recombination and efficient radiative recombination throughout the bulk; collectively, these morphological, optical, and structural signatures confirm that the optimized crystallization pathway intrinsically passivates undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ defects at grain surfaces and interfaces, enhances vertical charge transport, and minimizes interfacial energy disorder—resulting in VOC of 1.1256 V, JSC of 25.469 mA/cm², FF of 77.7608%, and PCE of 22.2927%.
